title: Drift on the Helm
text: The nav plot and the stars disagree by a hair, and the hair is growing. Somewhere in the gyro stack a reading has gone stale, and the ship is sliding a little further off her line every hour.
labels: Re-fix the plot against three stars
Nudge the trim until it looks right [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You shoot three stars, and then three more, and work the sums twice on paper before you trust them. The drift is a stale gyro, and you zero it. It takes most of a watch. (+3 experience at the pilot post.)
You trim by eye, and the line settles back almost where it should be. (+4 experience at the pilot post.)
You trim by eye and overshoot, and spend the next watch chasing your own correction back and forth. (+1 experience at the pilot post.)

title: Crowded Lane
text: A string of haulers has bunched up on the lane ahead, all at the same speed with the same idea. The nearest transponder is closing, and nobody on the band is giving way.
labels: Shave your burn and let them clear
Cut through the gap between two of them [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You trim the burn and fall back through the gap, and a minute later the lane has sorted itself out around you. Slower, and nobody swears at you. (+3 experience at the pilot post.)
You thread it, between two hulls with a few hundred meters each side, and come out the far end with your pulse going. (+4 experience at the pilot post.)
The gap closes faster than you judged, and you break off hard, with a lot of flashing lights and some language from the band. (+1 experience at the pilot post.)

title: The Docking Sim
text: The captain has left the approach for the next port on the sim, and said nothing about it. It is a hard one: a tight berth, a crosswind of station spin, and a score at the bottom of the screen with someone else's initials.
labels: Fly it slowly, until it is clean
Fly it at speed and see what happens [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You fly it five times, slowly, with the numbers up on the second screen, until the approach is clean in your hands. The initials at the bottom do not move, but you know why now. (+3 experience at the pilot post.)
You fly it hot, and it works, which surprises you more than anyone. The score is not the best, but it is close. (+4 experience at the pilot post.)
You fly it hot and hit the berth wall, and the sim sounds a rude tone. You reset it and do not look at the score. (+1 experience at the pilot post.)

title: The Flip Is Early
text: The captain's burn sheet puts the flip at the halfway mark. Your own numbers say the ship is carrying more speed than the sheet assumes, and the flip is ninety seconds early. Ninety seconds is a lot of reaction mass at the far end of a brake.
labels: Recompute the flip from the live numbers
Flip where the sheet says and correct on the brake [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You pull the live velocity, rerun the brake curve, and move the flip back by ninety-four seconds. You leave the captain a note with both figures. The ship arrives on the line with fuel to spare. (+3 experience at the pilot post.)
You flip at the sheet's mark and trim the brake by eye. The ship settles on the line with a little more fuel burned than you wanted. (+4 experience at the pilot post.)
You flip at the sheet's mark and overshoot the brake. You spend a long watch correcting, and the captain asks for the numbers. (+1 experience at the pilot post.)

title: A Return on the Plot
text: A faint return has been showing on the plot for an hour, small and slow, a little to port of the line. It could be a rock. It could be a ship running dark. Nobody else has mentioned it.
labels: Track it for another hour before you say anything
Call it a rock and let the plot go [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You track it for an hour, logging bearing and range every five minutes. It is a rock, tumbling, and it passes well clear. You write down the figures anyway. (+3 experience at the pilot post.)
You call it a rock and let it go, and it is a rock. You do not look at it again until it is behind you. (+4 experience at the pilot post.)

You call it a rock and stop watching. Forty minutes later it changes course. It is a small hauler running dark, and it passes close enough to read the paint. The captain finds out from the log. (+1 experience at the pilot post.)

title: A Jammed Feed
text: The ready rack has jammed, a round half in and half out, and the fire-control board is showing a fault in a color you have not seen. It will have to be cleared before anyone needs to shoot.
labels: Strip the feed and clear it by the book
Clear it with the manual override [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You safe the rack, strip the feed, and find a bent follower worn thin. You straighten it, oil the rest, and cycle the rack twenty times until it runs like a clock. (+3 experience at the gunner post.)
You hit the override and the round slams home with a clang. It runs, and keeps running. (+4 experience at the gunner post.)
The override seats the round crooked, and you have to take the whole feed apart anyway, now with a bruise. (+1 experience at the gunner post.)

title: Sights Out of True
text: The turret has been slewing a hair to the left for a week, and tonight you proved it on the range sim. Every shot lands wide by the same small amount.
labels: Boresight it against a fixed star
Apply a correction in the fire control [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You boresight it against a fixed star, slowly, one click at a time, until the cross and the star sit together and stay there. You log the offset for next time. (+3 experience at the gunner post.)
You dial in a correction by eye, and the next ten shots on the sim cluster neatly. It is not perfect, but it is close. (+4 experience at the gunner post.)
You dial in the correction the wrong way and it doubles the error. It takes an hour to find and undo. (+1 experience at the gunner post.)

title: Practice on the Range
text: The captain wants the guns run through their paces before the next port, and has left the range sim set to something unkind: fast targets, a lot of them, and a clock.
labels: Work the targets one at a time
Race the clock and take them as they come [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You take them one at a time, in order, ignoring the clock, and by the third pass the order has become instinct. The clock is still ahead of you, but you have stopped fighting it. (+3 experience at the gunner post.)
You race the clock and, for once, the targets just line up. You finish with seconds in hand and a ringing in your ears. (+4 experience at the gunner post.)
You lose the rhythm halfway through and the targets get ahead of you. You finish a long way behind the clock. (+1 experience at the gunner post.)

title: The Count Is Off
text: The magazine count on the board says four hundred rounds. The count you made by hand says three hundred and ninety. Someone has been in the rack, or the sensor has been lying, and either way the captain signs for the number on the board.
labels: Count the rack by hand, twice
Trust your count and correct the board [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You count the rack round by round, and then again. It is three hundred and ninety. You find a loose sensor lead on the rack and reseat it. The board and the rack agree. (+3 experience at the gunner post.)
You correct the board to your count and note why. The board agrees with the rack, and you log it. (+4 experience at the gunner post.)
You correct the board, and the sensor lead shorts. The board goes blank. You spend the rest of the watch counting again, by hand, with the captain watching. (+1 experience at the gunner post.)

title: Target Drone
text: The captain has launched a target drone, a battered orange canister, the only thing on the range worth shooting. It has been hit before. It is not meant to be hit twice in a burn. You have twenty minutes of range time.
labels: Take three shots and score each
Burst it and see what is left [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You take three shots with a full minute between them and score each against the telemetry. Two hit. You write down what the third missed by, and why. (+3 experience at the gunner post.)
You burst it, and the drone tumbles apart in a spray of orange. The captain gets the bill in the log. It was a good burst. (+4 experience at the gunner post.)
You burst it and miss with every round. The drone coasts on, unharmed, and the range clock runs out. (+1 experience at the gunner post.)

title: A Shudder in the Drive
text: There is a new sound in the drive room, a low, regular shudder at the edge of hearing that you feel in your back teeth. It comes and goes with the burn. Something is out of balance, and you are the one with the tools.
labels: Trace it through the mounts, one by one
Tighten what looks loose and listen [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You work down the mounts with a torque wrench and a hand on each, until you find the one that has crept loose. You reseat it, and the shudder stops. (+3 experience at the engineer post.)
You tighten the mount that looks loosest, and the shudder drops to a whisper and then goes. You write it down with a question mark. (+4 experience at the engineer post.)
You tighten the wrong one, and the shudder gets worse. You spend the rest of the watch finding the right one. (+1 experience at the engineer post.)

title: The Recycler Sulks
text: The air recycler has started to smell of hot dust, and its read-out has been stuck on one number for an hour. Nobody has said anything, but you have seen a few people breathing through their sleeves.
labels: Pull the cartridges and clean the whole stack
Swap in the spare cartridge [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You pull the cartridges, one at a time, and clean the stack down to bare metal. It takes the afternoon, and the air afterward is, noticeably, just air. (+3 experience at the engineer post.)
You swap in the spare, and the smell clears at once. The old one goes in the bin with a tag that says "check later". (+4 experience at the engineer post.)
The spare is the wrong size and takes a gasket to seat it. By the time it runs, you have lost the afternoon and a good deal of temper. (+1 experience at the engineer post.)

title: Warm Coolant
text: The coolant loop is running a few degrees warm. It is nowhere near a limit, but the trend is wrong, and you know a trend like that is a leak, or a pump, or a thing you have not thought of yet.
labels: Chase it from the pump to the radiator
Bleed the loop and hope [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You walk the loop from the pump to the radiator with a meter, and find a partly closed valve that someone, some time, nudged. You open it, and the loop settles. (+3 experience at the engineer post.)
You bleed the loop and top it up, and the temperature drops back. It does not feel like an answer, but it is a good enough one for now. (+4 experience at the engineer post.)
The bleed hisses and takes more than you wanted. The temperature drops, and so does the coolant level, and you spend an hour topping it up. (+1 experience at the engineer post.)

title: A Weep at the Hatch
text: There is a dark bead at the foot of the number two hatch seal, and a damp ring on the deck under it. It is coolant, or water, or something worse, and it was not there at the last port.
labels: Pull the seal and check the gasket
Wipe it and watch it [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You pull the seal and find the gasket flattened on one side, with a hair of grit under it. You clean the groove and fit a new gasket, and the deck stays dry. (+3 experience at the engineer post.)
You wipe it and watch it for a watch. It does not come back. You log the time and the place. (+4 experience at the engineer post.)
You wipe it and watch it. It comes back at the change of watch, and the bead is a trickle. You pull the seal after all, with the deck wet. (+1 experience at the engineer post.)

title: The Tripping Breaker
text: The breaker on the galley circuit has tripped three times since the flip. Each time it resets, and each time someone says it must be the kettle. It is not the kettle.
labels: Walk the circuit and test each load
Swap the breaker and see [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You walk the circuit with a meter and find a pinched cable behind the galley panel, shining where the insulation has rubbed through. You wrap it and reroute it, and the breaker holds. (+3 experience at the engineer post.)
You swap the breaker, and it holds all watch. You log it as probably the breaker. (+4 experience at the engineer post.)
You swap the breaker, and it trips again within the hour. This time the panel is warm. (+1 experience at the engineer post.)

title: Noise on the Band
text: There is a hiss on the band that was not there at the last port, rising and falling as the ship turns. It is stealing your range, and, if it is the antenna, it will only get worse.
labels: Walk the antenna run and check every join
Re-tune the filters and see [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You walk the whole run with a meter, join by join, and find a connector with a green crust on it. You clean it and re-seat it, and the band comes up clear and wide. (+3 experience at the comms post.)
You re-tune the filters, and the hiss drops out of the speech band like a stone out of a bucket. Good enough, you think, for now. (+4 experience at the comms post.)
You re-tune the filters and notch out half of someone's voice with the noise. You have to start again. (+1 experience at the comms post.)

title: A Garbled Hail
text: A hail comes in, at the very edge of range, stuttering and thick with static. A name, a transponder number and what could be a warning, or could be a tender asking for a berth. The captain would like to know which.
labels: Clean it up and read it properly
Guess at the gaps and answer [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You run the hail through every filter you have, a pass at a time, until a word comes out, and then a sentence. It is a tender asking for a berth. You log it and send the captain a note. (+3 experience at the comms post.)
You guess at the gaps and answer, and the voice on the other end relaxes at once. You guessed right. (+4 experience at the comms post.)
You guess wrong, and the voice on the other end goes cold, and starts again, slower. Your face is hot. (+1 experience at the comms post.)

title: The Day's Traffic
text: The log has built up: forty unread messages, six unanswered hails, and a list of stations that have, since the last port, changed their transponder codes without telling anyone.
labels: Go through it all, in order
Answer the urgent ones and skim the rest [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You work through it in order, and answer what needs answering, and file the rest. By the end you know the traffic in this part of the lane better than you did, and the log is clean. (+3 experience at the comms post.)
You answer the urgent ones and skim the rest, and nothing in the skim bites. A shortcut, and it holds. (+4 experience at the comms post.)
You skim past a notice that turns out to matter, and spend an hour working out what it said. (+1 experience at the comms post.)

title: Two Clocks
text: The station you are calling stamps its messages with a time that disagrees with the ship's clock by eleven minutes. One of them is wrong, and the log is full of messages stamped with whichever it is.
labels: Sync to three beacons and see which is wrong
Trust the station and adjust the offset [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You sync to three lane beacons. The ship's clock is the one that has drifted, by eleven minutes. You reset it and annotate every message since the last port. (+3 experience at the comms post.)
You apply the station's offset, and the log lines up. You note that you did not check. (+4 experience at the comms post.)

You apply the station's offset. The station was wrong. A message to the captain's broker goes out stamped eleven minutes in the future, and an answer comes back asking if it was a joke. (+1 experience at the comms post.)

title: A Relay Wants the Ship's Name
text: A relay buoy wants your transponder, your registry and your captain's name before it will pass your traffic. It is the right procedure. It is also more than the last three buoys asked.
labels: Ask the captain before you answer
Send what the last buoy got [if it fails: you learn less, and the captain marks it]

plays.text: You take it to the captain, who reads the request twice and tells you what to send and what not to. The buoy passes your traffic. The captain adds a line to the book. (+3 experience at the comms post.)
You send what the last buoy got. The buoy accepts it and passes your traffic, and nothing else happens. (+4 experience at the comms post.)
You send what the last buoy got. The buoy wants the rest, and your traffic sits in the queue for an hour while you ask the captain anyway. (+1 experience at the comms post.)

title: The Rock
text:
She is a dark lump on the board for three days, and then she is a mountain. A comet that lost its way, or a piece of one: black, pitted, with a white seam through it where the ice shows. There is no beacon, no berth, and nobody to ask. The captain brings the ship in to three kilometers and says what everyone is thinking, that you cannot dock with something that is tumbling.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.

The rock is bigger than the charts said, and it is turning, a long slow roll that takes eleven minutes. The ice is on the shadow side, a pale band between slabs of dust and rock. The captain has the ship stationed and the crew are at their suits. "Somebody tell me how we get close," the captain says.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.
labels: Match the roll and go in slow [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]
Go in fast, and brake hard [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty, and the captain marks it]
Send a line across first
[Pilot] Fly the approach by hand [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You match the roll over the course of an hour and come alongside at walking pace. The anchors bite on the first try.
The roll catches you out by a few degrees and a spur of rock clips the hull. The anchors hold, in the end. Armor -16.
You go in faster than anyone likes and brake at the last moment. You are on the ice with an hour in hand.
You come in too fast, and brake too late, and the hull takes a hit from the rock that rings every deck. Armor -31.
The line goes across and holds. You haul the ship in on it, a meter at a time, and no one has to be clever.
The line parts on the first haul. You spend two hours getting it across again.
You fly it by hand, with the drive cold, on the thrusters alone, in the shadow of the rock. The ship settles against the ice like something that belongs there.
The thrusters are not enough, and the rock turns into the ship. The paint will not forgive you. Armor -16.

Go in fast, and brake hard [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty, and the captain marks it]
Send a line across first
[Engineer] Set the anchors yourself [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You set the anchors in a pattern you worked out on the way: two forward, one aft, and a line for luck. The ship does not move.
An anchor fouls on a vein of rock and has to be cut away. You lose it and a morning. Armor -16.

Send a line across first
[Gunner] Blast a ledge to land on [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You put three shots into the dust at the rim, and the rock gives up a flat ledge with room for the ship. The captain says nothing, which is praise.
The shots bring down a slab that grazes the hull and spins away. You get a ledge, and a long list of things to fix. Armor -16.

Go in fast, and brake hard [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty, and the captain marks it]
Send a line across first
[Comms] Scan for the stable face [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You scan the rock for an hour and find the face that is not moving as much as the rest. The ship goes in there, and the anchors set at once.
The scan reads a quiet face that is a loose one. The anchors take, and then let go, and you start again. Armor -8.

title: Cutting Ice
text:
The cutters are out, six of them, and the white seam runs forty meters along the rock. The work is slow and cold and loud in the helmet: a saw to cut a block, a lift to carry it, the hold doors to put it in. It is the kind of work that goes right for an hour and wrong for a second. The captain has the ship on the radio and everyone else on the ice.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.

You are on the ice at the second shift, and the ship hangs above like a big dull star. The blocks are the size of a bunk, blue-white and very clean, and each one is worth more than a month of your wage. Someone on the radio says to watch the seam. It cracks while they are saying it.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.
labels: Cut small, and carry every block
Cut big, and use the lift [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty, and the captain marks it]
Work in pairs, and rotate every hour
[Pilot] Hold the ship steady over the seam [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You cut the blocks small and carry each one, and the hold fills steadily, with nothing lost and nothing hurt. The hold takes 26 tons of ice.
You cut small and carry everything, and the work is so slow that the light changes twice. The hold is not as full as it should be. The hold takes 22 tons of ice.
The big blocks come out clean and the lift takes them. The hold is full an hour early. The hold takes 30 tons of ice.
A big block shifts on the lift and takes the edge off the hold door. Nobody is under it, which is luck. Armor -21. The hold takes 18 tons of ice.
You work in pairs and rotate every hour. It is slower on paper, and nobody makes a mistake from tiredness. The hold takes 26 tons of ice.
The rotation is a good idea and the radio is bad. The pairs lose each other twice, and both times it ends well. The hold takes 22 tons of ice.
You hold the ship steady over the seam with the thrusters, in tiny pulses, so the lift can work from it. You do not blink for nine hours. The hold takes 30 tons of ice.
The ship drifts at the wrong moment, and the lift line goes taut. You catch it, but the hold door takes the strain. Armor -13. The hold takes 18 tons of ice.

[Engineer] Run the heaters off the drive [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You run a heat line from the drive to the cutters, so the blades do not freeze and the seam does not stick. The cutters sing. The hold takes 30 tons of ice.
The heat line takes more than you thought and the drive complains. You cut the power and lose an hour. Armor -16. The hold takes 18 tons of ice.

[Gunner] Use the guns to split the big slabs [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You split the big slabs with the guns, one shot at a time, along the seam. The blocks come away in clean pieces. The hold takes 30 tons of ice.
A shot goes into the wrong plane and the whole face shatters. It is a lot of ice, and not much of it is useful. Armor -16. The hold takes 18 tons of ice.

Work in pairs, and rotate every hour
[Comms] Keep the shifts on a schedule [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You keep every shift on the clock, call each handover, and track every block into the hold. The count at the end is exact, and the captain checks it twice. The hold takes 30 tons of ice.
You lose a shift in the schedule and two people on the ice at once. It is sorted out, and it is not forgotten. Armor -8. The hold takes 18 tons of ice.

title: Home With the Ice
text:
The hold is full, and the ship is heavy, and she burns like it. Every maneuver is slower, and every vibration matters, because there is a hundred tons of ice in the hold that is the only cargo you are being paid for. The captain has set a course for the buyer and a limit on the thrust, and has asked everyone to keep it in mind.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.

The rock is a pale dot astern, and then it is not. Nobody says anything for a while. The hold is full of water that will keep a dome alive for a month. It is a long way home, and the ship has never felt so slow.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.
labels: Keep the burn gentle and the hold cold
Burn hard, and trust the insulation [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty, and the captain marks it]
Stand watches on the hold
[Pilot] Fly the long way round, away from the lanes [if it fails: hull damage, a crew casualty]

plays.text: You keep the burn gentle and the hold cold, and the ice comes home as it left, in blocks, not in pools.
A gentle burn is a long one. The ice softens a little at the edges, and you lose a ton to the drains.
You burn hard, and the insulation holds. You gain two days, and the buyer is not asking where the time went.
The hard burn heats the hold wall, and a seam goes. You pump the water to the tanks, and lose some on the way. Armor -16.
You stand a watch on the hold all the way. Nothing goes wrong, because someone is looking at it.
Nobody wants the hold watch, and everyone takes it. It is a long, cold trip, and a quiet one.
You fly the long way, off the lanes, in the dark. Nobody finds you, and nobody is looking.
The long way is longer than the chart. You make the date by a day, and burn a lot of reaction mass doing it. Armor -10.

title: Home With the Ice
text:
The hold is full, and the ship is heavy, and she burns like it. Every maneuver is slower, and every vibration matters, because there is a hundred tons of ice in the hold that is the only cargo you are being paid for. The captain has set a course for the buyer and a limit on the thrust, and has asked everyone to keep it in mind.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.

The rock is a pale dot astern, and then it is not. Nobody says anything for a while. The hold is full of water that will keep a dome alive for a month. It is a long way home, and the ship has never felt so slow.

The haul so far: even. Armor 260/260.
